# Forecast Error Variance Decomposition


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
irf_response_test <- as.data.frame(theta_0)
irf_response_test$shock <- rep(names, length.out = length(theta_0[,1]))
irf_response_test$shock <- factor(irf_response_test$shock, levels = rev(names))
# fake plot just to construct the correct legend
colors_shock <- c("blue", "red", "green", "yellow")


plot_legend <- ggplot(data =irf_response_test, aes(x=V1, fill = shock))+
  geom_histogram()+
  theme( legend.direction = "horizontal")+
scale_fill_manual(
  values = rev(colors_shock),
  labels = TeX(rev(names)))
# Légende personnalisée (à ajuster selon vos besoins)
custom_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(plot_legend)
plot_legend
```



```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(latex2exp)

#names <- c("$Q_{elec}$" "$P_{elec}$" "IPI"        "$NE Index$")
plot_fevd <- function(series){
  
  decomp_tot_data <- data.frame(
    time= c(1:irhor),
    fevd[,series,])
  # Plot the decomposition
  colnames(decomp_tot_data)[-1] <- names
  
  # Reshaper les données en format long pour ggplot2
  library(tidyr)
  long_data <- pivot_longer(decomp_tot_data, 
                            cols = -time, names_to = "category",
                            values_to = "value")
  # S'assurer que 'category' a l'ordre des niveaux correspondant à 'colors_shock'
  # Modifier l'ordre des niveaux du facteur category
  long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = rev(names))
  
  # Tracer des barres empilées avec ggplot2
  my_plot <- ggplot()+
    geom_bar(data= long_data, aes(x = time, y = value, fill = category),
             stat = "identity", position = "stack") +  # Barres empilées
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = rev(colors_shock),
      labels = TeX(rev(names)))+
    #scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red", "green"), labels = c("Supply", "Demand", "Other")) +
    labs(#title=TeX(paste("Historical Decomposition of",names[[series]])) ,
         x="Time", y=TeX(names[series]))+
    theme(legend.position = "none")

  return(my_plot)
}
plot_fevd(1)


```



```{r}

# Apply the function to the sequence 3:10
results <- lapply(c(1:n) , plot_fevd)

# Arrange the plots in a grid
plots_grid <- do.call("grid.arrange", c(results, nrow = 2))

# Combine the grid with the legend
final_plot <- plot_grid(plots_grid, custom_legend, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))

title <- ggdraw() + 
  draw_label(TeX('Forecast Error Variance Decomposition'), fontface = 'bold', x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5)

# Combine the title and the final plot with legend
final_plot_with_title <- plot_grid(title, final_plot, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.1, 1))

# Display the final plot
print(final_plot_with_title)
```


```{r}
plot_fevd_iv <- function(series){
  
  decomp_tot_data <- data.frame(
    time= c(1:irhor),
    fevd_iv[,series,])
  # Plot the decomposition
  colnames(decomp_tot_data)[-1] <- names
  
  # Reshaper les données en format long pour ggplot2
  library(tidyr)
  long_data <- na.omit(pivot_longer(decomp_tot_data, 
                            cols = -time, names_to = "category",
                            values_to = "value"))
  # S'assurer que 'category' a l'ordre des niveaux correspondant à 'colors_shock'
  long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = rev(names))
  
  # Tracer des barres empilées avec ggplot2
  my_plot <- ggplot()+
    geom_bar(data= long_data, aes(x = time, y = value, fill = category),
             stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
    geom_line(data = long_data, aes(x=time, y=1), linetype='dashed')+
    # Barres empilées
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = rev(colors_shock[1:k]),
      labels = TeX(rev(names)))+
    #scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red", "green"), labels = c("Supply", "Demand", "Other")) +
    labs(#title=TeX(paste("Historical Decomposition of",names[[series]])) ,
         x="Time", y=TeX(names[series]))+
    theme(legend.position = "none")

  return(my_plot)
}
plot_fevd_iv(series = 1)
```



```{r}
# Apply the function to the sequence 3:10
results <- lapply(c(1:n) , plot_fevd_iv)

# Arrange the plots in a grid
plots_grid <- do.call("grid.arrange", c(results, nrow = 2))

# Combine the grid with the legend
final_plot <- plot_grid(plots_grid, custom_legend, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))

title <- ggdraw() + 
  draw_label(TeX('Forecast Error Variance Decomposition'), fontface = 'bold', x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5)

# Combine the title and the final plot with legend
final_plot_with_title <- plot_grid(title, final_plot, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.1, 1))

# Display the final plot
print(final_plot_with_title)
```
